findings: Offline thresholds and online per-token/per-group scale computation are separate; sampled distribution stability does not prove future-prompt invariance.

Dense slots use 4 bits per value, with 8 additional bits per outlier after fusion: ideal density 4+8p. Scales, thresholds, variable lengths, page tables and alignment remain additional. Six-bit index locality is not fully specified and is not invented here.
Dedicated DMA quantizer/dequantizer, sparse buffers and MMU overlap conversions. GPU implementation has divergence overhead; compressed capacity alone does not predict runtime.

Research evaluation uses extended LPU simulation, RTL functional verification and 28nm synthesis; it is not a measured production GPU implementation. Large A100 models use two-way PP, and several baselines are modified/unsupported.
Models are OPT/Llama2/Mistral/Mixtral, not V4/K3. One blanket Llama2 GQA statement is overbroad. Attention lacking inter-request KV reuse does not mean batching is impossible.
Figure 12(b) plots latency breakdown; Figure 13 plots sequence sweep, but their captions are swapped. No graph values adopted.
Quality-loss percentages use different baselines (0.87% vs FP16, 0.54% vs KVQuant). Table 4 percentages are compute-core area; estimated power versus A100 TDP is not matched measured energy.
Table 2 effective bit widths 4.82/4.89 differ from ideal 4.8 density; do not present payload algebra as complete measured allocation.
